verdict.tagline: Constant crashes and microtransactions drag down cooperative galactic warfare.
for_you_if: you can look past frequent technical instability
you enjoy cooperative squad-based PvE combat
you do not mind grinding for unlocks
not_for_you_if: you need stable frame rates and reliable game launches
you want Linux compatibility without anti-cheat blocks
you dislike aggressive microtransactions and paid warbonds

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game suffers from technical instability, including constant crashes, failure to launch past intro screens or black splash screens, and startup errors requiring troubleshooting steps like verifying files or clearing shader caches.

citations.review_text:
The game came out very poorly optimized. It was very laggy and very low frame rates. What really made me quit was the Into the Unjust update, which apparently damaged graphic cards for some players. My computer is my livelyhood (I work remote. Design). A game that breaks hardware is just unacceptable, especially for someone who lives off of their PC.
The game has had many updates since then, but after that presedent, they can't really go back into my good graces. It is just a risk I can't take.
Can't even get it to launch after the anti-cheat update. No mods installed, and fresh installation.

Incredible gameplay, but they are trying to polish and dress up a very large turd on a dead engine.
When this game actually works, it’s some of the most chaotic fun you can play. My frame rates are perfectly fine, but everything else surrounding the client is a complete and utter joke.

Every single patch is exhausting, and what i mean by that is when a new update drops, and instead of just playing, I’m forced into a frustrating routine of troubleshooting; uninstalling, wiping shader caches, and verifying game files just to get past a frozen black splash screen, or wait for it... A CRASH BEFORE IT EVEN LAUNCHES ITSELF!
We shouldn't have to act like IT support just to launch a game we paid for.

Like i said earlier, Arrowhead is trying to polish and dress up a very large turd of an 8-year abandoned and discontinued infrastructure. I want to love this game, but I’m sick of fighting the launcher more than the damn automatons. Buy it if you want great gameplay, but prepare to get intensely pissed off by the client. Thank you for coming to my [b] Beerus Talk. [/b]

Crashes on launch, fresh purchase and fresh install. Got it working after mucking around with different suggestions from the discussions. Played 3 rounds and then the whole thing got stuck on a black screen and needed to be force killed.
Can't recommend in its current buggy state.

constant crashes. constant bugs. i bought the game for 30$ and i am struggling to get at least 30 hours on it.
cant recommend it rn the anti cheat is buggy and makes the game crash

claims.claim: Reviewers describe mechanics where the game environment and systems actively hinder the player, such as unpredictable ragdolling, turrets targeting allies, and stratagem balls bouncing back.

citations.review_text: It is pretty clear by now that the developers intentionally want this game to be as frustrating to players as possible because they think it's funny for the characters to be bumbling buffoons that are in way over their head. Unfortunately that means they created a game environment with mechanics that frequently fight against the player to keep up the developer's vision. Mechanics like turrets shooting the player and their allies seemingly on purpose, stratagem balls bouncing around and dropping bombs on you, constantly being knocked down and thrown around by explosions and projectiles. I actually really like this game when it isn't fighting against me but Arrowhead works really hard to make sure that it always does.

Within 4 days of buying Helldivers 2, Arrowhead has already managed to:

Lie about the Major Order reward. It said the reward was going to be a stratagem, but then it turned out to be some reward for the DSS (which I still have no idea what even is). So essentially, the reward was nothing?? What a great first impression of the game and its developers!

And implement anti-cheat restrictions to prevent modding because apparently people were having too much fun playing a superior version of the game than AH themselves could develop. There seem to be bugs that have existed since the launch of the game that random vibe coders were able to easily fix, yet instead of implementing these fixes themselves, AH would rather just prevent these mods from functioning. Because they're jealous or something??

Besides that, the game itself has A LOT of potential, but it's just filled with problems that completely ruin the experience. There are so many bugs and janky mechanics that you constantly have to fight against the game itself rather than the enemies. Like the insane ragdolling that makes absolutely no sense and just takes control away from the player.

Then there's the awful predatory progression system that feels like something you'd find in a mobile game. This game costs 40 euros, yet what you get in the base game is so barebones it's actually ridiculous. A few primary weapons, TWO SECONDARIES, FOUR GRENADES. Everything else has to be grinded for.

And let's talk about the grind. For some reason, you don't get rewarded more Super Credits for playing on higher difficulties. On average, I get around 10–20 SC at difficulty 10 for each dive, and a single Warbond costs 1k SC. So the only way to get 1k SC within a reasonable amount of time is to waste 2–3 hours of your life playing on the lowest difficulty, mindlessly running around the map collecting this stupid currency instead of actually playing the game.

And then, when you finally have enough SC to buy the fucking Warbond, y…

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Anti-cheat updates cause performance drops and block Linux play, while weapon balancing and microtransactions frustrate progression.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the introduction of Easy Anti-Cheat causes launch failures, crashes, and performance drops.

citations.review_text:
A game I once enjoyed with friends has been completely ruined! After the last update, and so many different attempts at fixing the game, which we shouldn't have to do, I have had no luck in getting the game to boot up! 

My friend bought this game on Xbox recently because I wanted to enjoy it with them while on PC, thanks to crossplay. Today, we went to boot it up and on PC it wouldn't load - Xbox was fine. 

Big thumbs down for a game that was once a thumbs up! Uninstalled for now, don't have time to waste fixing something that never needed fixing...

Was a good game...

Why does anti-cheat even matter in a co-op non-competitive game...?

The only thing that has changed for me with them changing anti-cheats is that now I CAN'T LAUNCH THE GAME.  I just get an error.  Never had an issue with cheating before...  cause again... it's not a competitive game.

Good game, but the latest update introducing the new anti-cheat system unfortunately broke it.
I can no longer boot Helldivers 2 up, and no solution seems to fix the problem. gg arrowhead.

Easy Anti-Cheat has made my game unplayable. Crash on start lmao

Never had crashing issues before this awful update.

I can no longer play after the latest EAC update as I crash upon landing in game. Regardless of which version of proton I use or if I verify game files and I have also updated my drivers. I have never used any mods. Thank you Easy Anti-cheat.
woah new update that should only affect people who run mods. Oh it drops my frames to ~70 from ~180, and causes the game to crash constantly.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that an update introducing Easy Anti-Cheat blocked community mods and made the game unplayable on Linux.

citations.review_text:
Guess I'm not allowed to play this game anymore since it seems Arrowhead removed the ability for the game to run under Linux or VMs after switching the anticheat engine to EAC (and I happen to game under a Linux VM).

Thanks Arrowhead, I'll be sure to keep this in mind during my future game purchases.

Despite my relatively short playtime, I have some very strong opinions on this game.

Namely the grind. It is absolutely absurd how much you need to grind as a new player to unlock fun items.

First of all, you need to grind a thousand super credits to unlock a warbond. 1500 if it's a crossover one. This takes fucking forever, and the grind to getting super credits is completely unfun, even if you get a mod that shows all the super credit locations on the map. They usually come in batches of 10, and there's normally only a handful of pickups per match.

After you've sat through that arduous grind, you finally get the privilege of, guess what, grind even more! You need to grind through and waste hundreds of medals to get to the stuff in the warbond which you actually want to have. You need to go through 3 layers of grinding before you're even allowed to grind for the item that you actually want.

Just about everything you might want to play with in this game is locked behind this ridiculously long grind. And until you get these items, you are virtually dead weight on missions that are even halfway up the difficulty gauge.

To make this even worse, Arrowhead just released an update which has virtually bricked the game for me on Linux. Even without any mods enabled at all, it always crashes less than ten minutes into a mission. All to make sure people can't use quality of life mods.

I sorely regret spending money on this game. Ever since I bought it, it's done nothing but spit in my face and demand I waste more time and money just to enjoy the game I paid for.

For the record, this is a great game. And one I planned to put a lot more time into.
But as of the most recent update, the devs decided to add EAC, two years into the games life cycle. This isn't a PVP game, it's a co-op horde shooter, but the devs are seemingly allergic to fun, as we're all aware of their notorious treatment and constant nerfs of fun/good weapons.
Being a Linux user, I'm unable to even launch the game anymore, I've no doubt a workaround will be found, but this is such a ludicrous decision by the devs. The constant disconnect between them and their playerbase is frankly outstanding.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe weapon balancing as frustrating, noting that frequent nerfs make weapons unusable in this cooperative PvE game.

citations.review_text:
I cannot in good conscience recommend this game wholeheartedly in its current state. For context, I was a PS5 Helldivers player who played from release and spent hundreds of hours on the game. However, I was forced to move to PC because of PlayStation’s predatory subscription model, which forces players who already bought the game to pay an additional fee just to access it. Eventually, the subscription costs more than the game itself.

Why do I not recommend it? You sink hours of your life into this game—maybe even spend extra money on a Warbond to have fun—only to have enemies buffed or weapons nerfed in a PvE game that isn't even a competitive multiplayer experience. I also have to question what the Galactic War and the overarching story are actually about at this point. At every major turning point, there is very little payoff, and creative narrative elements are completely ignored or never implemented. It makes you question the point of sinking hours into completing a campaign. On top of those issues, frequent updates and nerfs either break the game or make it swing wildly between feeling trivial and immensely difficult. Don't waste your time or money if you can spend it on real-life necessities or actual long-term games with a rewarding payoff.

A separate issue is the community, which has transformed into a toxic cesspool where people can't even agree on a safe space or channel. I was personally deeply discouraged by the charity challenge incident, where someone's entire life was ruined over a playful charity event and Arrowhead made no attempt to step in. Even if the harassment happened outside the game environment, reaching out to the affected person's job or family would have been a show of good faith, yet that didn't happen. It makes you question the authenticity of their in-game charity campaigns. If they truly support players and charitable causes, wouldn't it have made sense to reach out? I'm not saying the charity itself is bad, but I am questionin…

I can't comprehend how a studio can be this fucking stupid and have such a fragile ego.
55hrs and even I can see this things...
1. Years without fixing game-breaking bugs.
2. A complete lack of understanding of their own game, to the point where modders fixed problems in a matter of days.
3. Updates that introduce EAC and tank game performance, while breaking mods that add features that should have been in the game since launch.
4. Alienating their own player base by telling players that they don't understand how the game is supposed to be played.
5. Doubling down on their "grunt fantasy" until the game becomes an absolute chore to play, bugs included.
6. Brain-dead balance changes that punish players for being creative and finding effective strategies.

For the record, I enjoy playing Level 10 dives. I like the challenge. But if I'm forced to use only three viable weapons to have a reasonable chance of succeeding because everything else has either been nerfed into the ground or rendered unusable by a bug or glitch that Arrowhead apparently didn't like players exploiting, then that's just bad game design.

If Arrowhead expects us, to be stupid enough not to notice that so many of these changes seem designed to prove the developers right rather than improve the game, then they clearly don't deserve our time or money.

DON'T MAKE THE SAME MISTAKE LIKE THE REST OF US. DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME OR MONEY ON THIS EXCUSE FOR A GAME THAT CLAIMS TO CARE ABOUT ITS PLAYERS AND THEIR EXPERIENCE.

P.S. This EAC update feels like an excuse for Arrowhead to shut down modding, including mods that objectively improve the game. It honestly wouldn't surprise me if they're just butthurt that modders managed to fix problems the developers themselves claimed they couldn't find solutions for.

For the record, this is a great game. And one I planned to put a lot more time into.
But as of the most recent update, the devs decided to add EAC, two years into the games life cycle. This isn't a PVP game, it's a co-op horde shooter, but the devs are seemingly allergic to fun, as we're all aware of their notorious treatment and constant nerfs of fun/good weapons.
Being a Linux user, I'm unable to even launch the game anymore, I've no doubt a workaround will be found, but this is such a ludicrous decision by the devs. The constant disconnect between them and their playerbase is frankly outstanding.

The devs have a backwards way of balancing, One prime example of this is their need to hide balancing from you. Plenty of things have either gotten shadow nerfed from the players side or shadow buffed from the enemy side. While its gotten better, undocumented changes still happen way more than they should. 
It's not the end of the world, but its a frustrating part that takes them a long time to adress and in most cases they only do so in the official discord. 

They also have a fundamental disconnect between what the community wants in terms of content and balancing.

But that's not my largest grievance with the game, my largest grievance is the monitization. 
When the game launched, it was all fine and dandy, grind SC or spend a little money to get a singular warbond which made it a fair way to balance free with paid content. 

But now? 

Now its a upward hill struggle for anyone new to the game, or anyone who took breaks because AH pumps out warbonds so frequently its honestly astonishing. And because there is basically no progression system past the very early stages there are no other ways to earn weapons, armors, strategems etc, without running the current war campaign, which if you miss by any reason will force you to wait months for the item in that to re-release.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that premium Warbonds cost real money or require extensive grinding, with a significant portion of the game's content locked behind them.

citations.review_text:
I'm definitely not the first person to bring these things up, but I'd still like to throw in my two cents.

Between the large amount of paid content, the growing distrust of the developers, and the recent introduction of Easy Anti-Cheat, I believe I would be right in saying that right now, Helldivers 2 is in a pretty rough state.

As of me writing this, a majority of the content released in Helldivers 2 is tied to a paywall. 'Warbonds' as they're called. You get one for free, the other 24 cost $10-20 per Warbond. 80% of your progression in this game is tied to a premium currency which is neither fun nor easy to grind for. 

Then there's the rift between the playerbase and the developers.
For a while now, there has been a growing amount of frustration within the community of Helldivers 2 over a perceived lack of honesty, or caring for that matter, from the developers, Arrowhead Studios. The devs say they won't nerf a certain weapon, only to then nerf it indirectly. They said they would dial back ragdolling on the Automaton front, only to introduce the warstrider, an extremely annoying enemy that practically specializes in just that. The devs would say they can't add a feature due to limitations within the game engine... and then modders would do it themselves.

And, finally the most recent addition to the game along side the new Scope of Authority Warbond: Easy Anti Cheat. Arrowhead had multiple options to deal with their modding community, and they chose the worst one. They could have made separate lobbies for people with mods, added a mod menu for approved addons, but instead they chose exterminatus and blamed it on cheaters.

Do you get me?

I don't hate the developers, and I doubt the other veteran players do either. However, Arrowhead keeps making promises to make Helldivers 2 better, and for every step taken forward, they've taken two back.
I'll believe it when I see it.

Do not buy this game, atleast at the time of me writing this review. The game's got a few very big problems, a major one being the warbond system. ArrowHead locks armors, weapons, and many other things behind warbonds on a game that already costs 40 dollars. Now, you *COULD* get these warbonds for free... Thats if, your willing to do unfun grinding that lasts literal days. Its a free to play strategy on a game thats quite the opposite. Other than that, ArrowHead also has a tendency of releasing updates that are just not fun and can ruin the experience for some, constantly buffing enemies and nerfing player equipment, and above that, the game has become less optimized overtime.  Unless either they get better, or you can get this game for free or at a lower price, it is not worth buying. There are alot more things I can mention here that I wont go into, if you are considering buying this game, I suggest doing more research into it's problems.

Amazing game
Horrible devs ( sometimes )

Is HD2 worth getting into at this time? I think so
Does arrowhead need to fix their damn game? Oh hell yes.

Helldivers 2 is such an amazing game. And i dont think i've had such fun playing with friends and solo in a long time. It's one of those games where even a horrible and frustrating mission can still be fun if you're screwing about with friends. It's incredibly cinematic, and results in such amazing moments that probably 100GB of my storage is dedicated to helldiver clips alone.

There is quite some content, though most locked behind "Super Credits" the games virtual premium currency. 
This in itself is... Fine... HD2 is a live service game and needs a constant influx of cash to stay viable. Though I wouldn't complain if the game's economy was made a *tad* less grindy. 

Super Credits are scattered throughout most HD2 maps. Even if it's a little. ( It's up to chance regarding how many spawn ) which makes players capable of acquiring this virtual currency for "free". 

I say "Free" because you're still spending more than a couple hours of your life mindlessly grinding for that one warbond you want. Speaking off...

Warbonds in their current state are... Okay. I think they're a good idea. But holy cow are they ridiculously expensive. 

10 euros for a standard premium warbond.
15 euros for a legendary warbond. ( warbonds that feature a collab between Helldivers and other games like warhammer 40k and halo. )

I am fortunate enough to be in a position where I can afford those prices. But I know many of us are not, and I don't agree with their exclusion from otherwise great content. Yes you can technically play this game without needing to unlock any warbonds. But lets be honest to ourselves, a lot of fun content IS locked behind a paywall. Be it paid with money or time... You will have to pay.

That brings me onto my last point, the developers themselves. And oh boy... Do I have something to say for you, arrowhead.

I under…

The devs really seem to want to fight their playerbase on what is good for the game. They constantly push updates that really don't mesh well with the game then end up walking them back weeks later.

The game is pay to play but expect to spend another $60 on DLC and another $10 every other month just to have access to the new stuff, or farm the premium currency for 10 hours anytime a new warbond drops.

Players want cosmetics? new warbond drops that offers some very minimal cosmetics on items in that warbond
Players complain about ragdoll? increase ragdoll then put an armor in the new warbond that reduces ragdoll
Mods fix major QOL issues and give the hint of visual cosmetics? nuke mods install new anticheat.

All this being said I really love the gameplay i just wish that the devs weren't constantly trying to get another $10 out of me while telling me that I'm not their target audience and that the game where you have 20 respawns a mission is a milsim.

If you don't love the gameplay it's a pass but I like it so i'd recommend it with a grain of salt.

Early on it was a 9/10 game but dev choices over it's life have put it at a 7/10 and I haven't put more than purchase and $20 for war bonds into it since release.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe long-standing technical issues and unaddressed bugs, including broken hellpod steering, stratagem balls bouncing randomly off flat surfaces, and inconsistent enemy collision detection.

citations.review_text: I loved and enjoyed this game for a while. I can no longer enjoy the game, this frustration has been building up since they continually refuse to bring out QoL updates, with Strategem bouncing (I know its intended; I could careless, it's a bad decision), vaulting/mantling being broken almost 2 years, Bad hellpod steering & rng spawn areas, and never ending mob cliping issues. With canning amazing ideas like the Platoon system, armour customization and Strategems Launchers. Plus no Server/Global chat sucks no way to organize outside of 3rd party sites. The final nails being the false advertising of the new warbond, Making non cheat Mods unplayable, Easy anti cheat breaking the game as usual; not allowing it to run properly/crashing/failing to launch. Its pains me but I find no joy in playing the game anymore. So heres how to fix the game and save it, AH please.. REMOVE EASY ANTI CHEAT ITS A PIECE OF GARBAGE, I'm tired of trouble shooting/reinstalling the game everytime I want to launch the game. Fix all above issues stated. ADD the Platoon system please and allow massive platoons to have platoon regulated DSS' and server/global chat. Buff some of the old under powered weapons show them some love! Buff the turret radius of the maelstrom TD to match the guided missile radius or slightly under it. Add a Main battle tank with a full 360 turret radius w/ an additional manned turret for one of the passenger seats. ADD LOADOUTS PLEASE like 8+ loadout slots. I'm probably forgetting other things but I'm tired Grandpa I don't wanna dig no more holes...

I have spent a lot of time playing this game.  The visuals, fun playing with friends, and great gameplay kept me coming back for a long time.  The game developers are artists.  They made the art they wanted.  

They seem to have no desire to actually fix anything that the players feel is an issue.   Whether it was hellpod steering, strategem bouncing, enemies shooting through bushes or bodies (that the player can't shoot through),  or constant levels of fog so the player can't see more than 10 feet in front of them, Arrowhead (the developer of Helldivers 2) seems to have no interest in fixing any of it.  

There are still no signs of simple things like armor appearance customization, armor bonus movement (from one set to another), saved loadouts,  full weapon customization for all weapons, despite these being the most requested improvements / mods from players.
 
In addition to not having a desire to fix any of these aforementioned issues Arrowhead have a string of out right lies (Coyote nerfs) hidden changes to the game and broken promises of roadmaps, fixes, or apologies.  Arrowhead seems to have a pathological need to nerf things that players enjoy or find engaging.  

When modders began to fix / mod things within the game that players wanted, Arrowhead quickly took steps to break those mods and in my opinion lied about why they were changing the anti-cheat program.  

I'm just tired of Arrowhead's lies, their continual treatment of the player base with contempt and their lack of professionalism or care.  If there was some drastic course change or new management,  I'd potentially be willing to come back, but for a good while... I'm just over it.

Cracking down on mods instead of actually fixing issues in the game we have requested for 2 years is a real kick on the balls. 

-Stratagem ball bouncing
-Excessive ragdoll
-Excessive volumetric fog spam that makes the game run worse
-Being unable to mix and match armor and armor passives
-Hellpod steering locking up forcing you to land where the game wants you to go, often leading you to your death
-Inconsistent Vaulting
-Enemy Collison not matching what you see 
-Being unable to promote other players as squad leader or to disband squads
-Can't match armor/helmet colors
-So many terrible weapons that could use a buff like the M90a, AR One-Two, Arbitrator, Variable, etc.

Side Note : The M6C/SOCOM doesn't even have the smart optic that is does in Halo 3 ODST. I feel like I have been robbed, Twice. First, purchasing the ODST wardbond as my first one because I am a massive Halo fan, only to be disappointed that it doesn't have the smart optic. The second time, AH is gonna prevent me from using the mod that adds the smart optic to the gun. The M6C/SOCOM could have been a far more a unique sidearm by having both the suppressor and scope than just a peacemaker with more damage with a suppressor. 

AH could've embraced the mods and have mod support. There could have been workshop support, L4D2 is still thriving to this day. AH could've just had public Vanilla lobbies separate from Modded ones, Baldur's Gate 3 has this! You can filter out Modded online lobbies for a pure vanilla experience.

After years of diving, the new anti-cheat switch to Easy Anti-Cheat and the crackdown on mods is the final straw. 

Arrowhead has spent more energy blocking community fixes than actually fixing their own game.

Long-standing bugs that modders solved in days or weeks (better stratagem ball bounce, unlocked hellpod steering, shallow water diving, consistent large-enemy corpse collisions, ragdoll sticking, and more) have sat unaddressed by Arrowhead for years. These weren’t cheats—they were basic quality-of-life repairs that made the game functional.

The existence of these mods is living proof of Arrowhead’s incompetence. A single dedicated modder (and the broader community) repeatedly delivered the exact fixes players begged for while the studio formed councils, issued vague statements, and shipped more broken balance patches and warbonds.

Gameplay-affecting mods that improved the experience for everyone are now getting killed alongside actual cheats. 

Cosmetic and pure QoL tools will break or require constant rework, while core problems (strat bouncing, invisible corpses, collision desync, etc.) return full force.

The original GameGuard was so ineffective that cheaters and exploiters ran wild for ages. 
Switching to EAC now feels less like protecting the Galactic War and more like punishing the community that kept the game alive by papering over Arrowhead’s failures.

Balance, performance, and basic polish remain inconsistent. Players still deal with the same frustrating systems the studio has known about forever, yet the priority is shutting down the tools that made the game tolerable.


Helldivers 2 had (and still has) incredible potential, but Arrowhead keeps proving they would rather restrict the community than learn from it. Mods didn’t ruin the game—Arrowhead’s inability to ship proper fixes did. This anti-cheat move just makes it official.

There is no other words than "Sheer Developer Incompetence" when it comes to Helldivers 2. Let me be real with you, you dont need a taskforce to get it fixed by the end of the year, a competent dev team would get it fixed, and this is generous of my part, within a month or two, but they didn't even get that time window, having to wait till the end of the year to resolve bugs that is being talked and talked over and over again to the death instead of fixing it is a shame and you shouldn't be a developer to the game. And to add more salt to the injure, there is a competent dev team on other games, Warframe devs wouldnt have these bugs sit in the game for months to almost a year, they would have it fixed within the hour with a hotfix or within a week where the next game patch with bugfixes drops.
